'''Shoshana Kamin''' ({{langx|ru|Шошана Камин}}, {{langx|he|שושנה קמין}}) (born December 24, 1930),<ref name="biobib">See reference {{harv|Fomin|Shilov|1969|p=562}}.</ref> born '''Susanna L'vovna Kamenomostskaya''' ({{langx|ru|Сусанна Львовна Каменомостская}}),<ref name="biobib"/><ref>See her paper {{harv|Kamin|1976|p=171}} and [http://www.mathnet.ru/php/person.phtml?personid=39913&option_lang=eng her author page] at [[All-Russian Mathematical Portal]].</ref> is a [[Soviet Union|Soviet]]-born [[Israel]]i [[mathematician]], working on the theory of [[parabolic partial differential equation]]s and related [[mathematical physics]] problems.

== Biography ==
Shoshana Kamin graduated from [[Moscow University]] in 1953 and earned her "[[candidate of science]]" degree from the same university in 1959,<ref name="biobib"/>  under the supervision of [[Olga Oleinik]].<ref>See the list of [[Olga Oleinik]] [[Candidate of Sciences]] students in {{harv|Venttsel'|Vladimirov|Zhikov|Il'in|2003|p=171}} (Russian version).</ref>
She and her two sons left the Soviet Union in the early 1971. After that she became a professor in [[Tel Aviv University]],<ref>See {{Harvtxt|Milman|2006|p=217}}. He precisely states:-"''The emigration of the mid-1970s had already brought mathematicians of the highest caliber and of all ages to Israel: Mikhail Lifshits and  David Milman, Israel Gohberg and Il'ya Pyatetskii-Shapiro, Shoshana Kamin, Boris Moishezon, Yurii Gurevich and I (I include myself in this group).''"</ref> where she is now [[professor emeritus]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.tau.ac.il/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=3&Itemid=13|title=List of senior faculty members at the School of Mathematical Sciences|publisher=Tel Aviv University}}</ref>

==Contributions==
In the late 1950s, she gave the first proof of the existence and uniqueness of the [[generalized solution]] of the three-[[dimension]]al [[Stefan problem]].<ref>See references {{harv|Kamenomostskaya|1961}} and {{harv|Oleinik|1960}}, as well as the historical survey on the [[Stefan problem]] in {{harv|Rubinstein|1971|pp= 1–15}}.</ref> Her proof was generalised by Oleinik.<ref>See {{harvtxt|Oleinik|1960}} and {{harvtxt|Rubinstein|1971|pp= 1–15 and 310}}.</ref>

Later, she made important contributions to the study of the [[porous medium]] equation,<ref>See {{harvtxt|Vázquez|2007|p=15}}.</ref>

:<math> \partial_t u = \Delta_x u^m, \,\, m > 1, </math>

and to non-linear elliptic equations.<ref>See {{harvtxt|Rădulescu|2007|p=22}}.</ref>

The "''Mathematics in the [[USSR]] 1958–1967''" is a two–volume continuation of the opus "''Mathematics in the [[USSR]] during its first forty years 1917–1957''" and describes the developments of Soviet mathematics during the period 1958–1967. Precisely it is meant as a continuation of the second volume of that work and, as such, is titled "''Biobibliography''" (evidently an [[acronym]] of [[biography]] and [[bibliography]]). It includes new biographies (when possible, brief and complete) and bibliographies of works published by new Soviet mathematicians during that period, and updates on the work and biographies of scientist included in the former volume, alphabetically ordered with respect to author's surname.
